stories.title: Algae based building materials market projected to 2035
stories.summary: The global market for algae-based building materials is transitioning from a niche sector to a commercially viable component of the construction industry, according to IndexBox. The report cites broader demand fundamentals and a more regionally diversified supply architecture. The sector now looks toward a 2035 forecast horizon.

stories.title: Agricultural waste repurposed for structural masonry
stories.summary: Researchers Abhishek Kumar and Raju Ranjan Kumar demonstrated that agricultural combustion residues can be used in structural masonry. Replacing ten percent of fly ash with agricultural ash and natural fibres yielded compressive strengths comparable to conventional bricks. The study suggests agro-waste can maintain standard density and absorption thresholds.

stories.title: Transparent bamboo and solar PV design for skylights
stories.summary: Researchers at India’s Vellore Institute of Technology have designed a glazing system combining transparent wood with transparent solar PV modules. The system uses a solar layer to generate electricity and a wood layer to block interior heat gain. The wood is rendered transparent by removing light-absorbing lignin.

stories.title: India faces multi-trillion dollar net zero financing gap
stories.summary: India requires $22.7 trillion to reach net zero by 2070, according to a CFA Society India analysis. The report identifies a financing gap of $2.5 trillion by 2050, which is expected to grow to $6.5 trillion by 2070. Most of this shortfall is currently expected to be debt.

stories.title: IGBC to host 24th Green Building Congress in Mumbai
stories.summary: The Indian Green Building Council marks 25 years with over 20,620 registered projects covering 16.55 billion square feet. The organization will host its 24th Green Building Congress in Mumbai from November 26 to 28, 2026. The event theme focuses on building greener worlds together.

stories.title: Moab academic building achieves zero energy certification
stories.summary: Utah State University’s Moab Academic Building has achieved Zero Energy Certification from the International Living Future Institute. Designed by Lake Flato Architects, the facility uses building orientation and deep overhangs to manage temperatures. The design relies on principles used by ancestral Puebloans to handle extreme desert heat.

stories.title: Green Bengal Summit focuses on resilient urban growth
stories.summary: The IGBC Green Bengal Summit 2026 addressed sustainable and climate-resilient urbanisation in West Bengal. Minister Agnimitra Paul advocated for green development across Durgapur, Asansol, Howrah and Siliguri. Officials stated that future-proofing is now an essential economic and environmental prerequisite for the state's urban development projects.

stories.title: Cambridge Central Mosque receives sustainable building award
stories.summary: The Cambridge Central Mosque won an award for its eco-friendly design at an international competition during COP31. The mosque is described by supporters as Europe’s first environmentally friendly mosque. This latest recognition brings the total number of awards received by the building to 24.

stories.title: IGBC reports 20,620 registered green building projects
stories.summary: The Indian Green Building Council reports that India is the world's second-largest green building market, with 20,620 registered projects covering 16.55 billion square feet. The organisation will hold its 24th Green Building Congress in Mumbai from November 26 to 28 to discuss the transition toward net zero cities.

stories.title: Green Buildings: Building a Sustainable Future for India - Realty Plus Magazine
Restoration of Udayagiri temple complex underway
stories.summary: Restoration work at the Sri Ranganayakula temple in Andhra Pradesh aims to conserve the structure while maintaining its original construction language. The project seeks to preserve the historic Vaishnava shrine, which includes high-walled enclosures and halls, as it recovers architectural evidence of the site's past as a community centre.

stories.title: Indian architect wins global golf design award
stories.summary: Aashish Vaishnava has become the first Indian to receive the World Golf Awards’ Golf Course Designer of the Year title. He shared the 2026 global award with British partner Jon Hunt. The winners were announced at a ceremony in Egypt on November 7.

stories.title: India Biennale to host installations at historic sites
stories.summary: The second edition of the India Art, Architecture and Design Biennale will run from December 4, 2026, to March 21, 2027. The 108-day event will feature installations at Delhi heritage sites including the Red Fort and Purana Qila. The number 108 was chosen for its traditional significance.

stories.title: AD Design Show 2026 opens in Mumbai
stories.summary: The AD Design Show 2026 opened on November 13 at the Jio World Convention Centre in Mumbai. The event featured a keynote address from editorial and industry partners, alongside various brand activations. The show is held in association with several design and surface material companies.

stories.title: IIM Bangalore earns platinum green campus certification
stories.summary: IIM Bangalore has received Platinum certification under the IGBC Green Campus Rating System. It is the first educational institution in India to earn this distinction. The rating recognises the campus for its energy efficiency, water conservation, renewable energy use and sustainable management practices.

stories.title: Survey of contemporary Indian architecture published
stories.summary: The Built99 project has released a survey featuring 99 architectural practices. The collection aims to provide an overview of contemporary Indian architecture through the work of these firms.

stories.title: Bengaluru resort features man-made underground architecture
stories.summary: Guhantara, located on Kanakapura Road, is marketed as India's first man-made underground cave resort. The property features subterranean accommodation, a spa and swimming facilities. The design translates ancient forms of shelter into a hospitality experience by placing the resort within the earth.

stories.title: Pune apartment design adapts to potential future expansion
stories.summary: Sanjay Puri Architects designed a 5,000-square-foot Pune apartment with the possibility of connecting it to an adjacent home in the future. The designers aimed to balance the parents' conservative sensibility with a hint of modernity, while incorporating existing furniture pieces into the new layout.

stories.title: Minthis resort development in Paphos
stories.summary: Cypriot developer Pafilia and Woods Bagot have completed Minthis, a resort-style development in the hills of Tsada Village. The project includes master planning, architecture, and branding services to create a retreat experience that combines local antiquity with premium amenities. The site covers five million square metres.

stories.title: Sustainable boarding school dormitories in Brazil
stories.summary: Architects have added two dormitory villages to the Canuanã school in Tocantins, Brazil, to house 540 pupils. The structures use locally sourced timber and earth bricks, featuring a vast canopy for shade and perforated walls for ventilation. The project aims to demonstrate how sustainable buildings can be beautiful.

stories.title: Japanese sauna designed to dissolve into the forest
stories.summary: Daichi Inc has completed the Daichi Silent River Tree Sauna in Kanagawa, Japan. The structure uses tree trunks as supports to make the architecture feel like part of the forest. The studio claims the design makes people feel as though they are dissolving into the woodland environment.

stories.title: Limestone wall protects jaguar habitat in Mexico
stories.summary: Mexican studio Colectivo C733 has constructed an 18-kilometre limestone wall at Parque del Jaguar in Tulum. The project aims to protect over 1,000 hectares of forest from development and tourism while allowing wildlife to pass through. It replaces a conventional enclosed nature reserve with a network of access points.

stories.title: Kengo Kuma and the quiet landscape
stories.summary: Architect Kengo Kuma has built a career on quiet, low-profile structures after being inspired by the Yoyogi National Gymnasium in 1964. His work, ranging from restaurants to public spaces, is defined by a character that avoids grand gestures, making his buildings easy to admire from a distance.

stories.title: Kengo Kuma completes circular thatched house in Japan
stories.summary: Kengo Kuma and Associates has finished the Kagaku no Sato Main House in Ibaraki Prefecture. The project features a circular thatched roof and 3D-scanned timber construction. It recently received the Encouragement Award at the Wood Design Awards 2026. The roof curves upward as if lifted by wind.

stories.title: Friendship Centre wins inaugural MoMA architecture prize
stories.summary: Kashef Chowdhury/URBANA has won the inaugural Ambasz to MoMA Annual Prize for Nature-Reconciled Architecture for its Friendship Centre in Bangladesh. The $200,000 award recognizes projects that address the relationship between built and natural environments. Half of the prize money is allocated to a non-profit organization for tree planting.

stories.title: Al Jahili Fort cooling project
stories.summary: A 2007 conservation project installed a network of chilled-water pipes beneath the mud plaster of the 1890s Al Jahili Fort in Al Ain. The engineering allows the mud-brick structure to function as a year-round cultural destination despite summer temperatures reaching 50°C. The fort was built by Zayed the First.

stories.title: JSWD to design RIYMAR Towers in Riyadh
stories.summary: German practice JSWD has won an international competition to design the RIYMAR Towers in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia. The mixed-use project will include residential, hospitality, office, and retail space. It is positioned as part of the broader urban transformation outlined in the Saudi Vision 2030 development plan.

stories.title: Arudeko creates material from waste wool
stories.summary: Mexican studio Arudeko has developed Bianni, a paper-like material made from waste wool sourced from local weaving communities. The textile is created by weaving dyed wool off-cuts with recycled paper. The resulting material can be sculpted into items such as lampshades and room dividers to reduce textile waste.

stories.title: Callaway invests in Texas 3D printing facility
stories.summary: Callaway Golf Company has committed $15 million to a 3D printing facility in Fort Worth, Texas. The site will focus on titanium R&D and manufacturing for custom club designs that conventional methods cannot produce. Operations are expected to begin in mid-2027, with custom product manufacturing starting in 2028.

stories.title: Icon 3D-prints commercial center in San Antonio
stories.summary: Austin-based Icon is using a robotic printer to construct a 12,649-square-foot training and exhibition center for ASCO Equipment in San Antonio. The project marks the company's largest commercial building to date. The facility will include an open training floor, tiered seating, and an upstairs lounge for equipment testing.

stories.title: ETH Zurich researchers test bacteria building materials
stories.summary: Karen Antorveza Paez at ETH Zurich is researching whether microorganisms can act as collaborators in architecture. The method combines living bacteria, sand, and digital fabrication to create mineral structures without heat-intensive kilns. The research aims to push the boundaries of robotic dexterity and complex material development in construction.

stories.title: Magnesium slag shows potential for low-carbon concrete
stories.summary: A systematic review suggests industrial magnesium slag can serve as a binder in cementitious materials. By using accelerated carbonation curing and mechanochemical activation, the metallurgical residue can reach optimal mechanical strength. The process offers a way to transform underutilized waste into a component for eco-friendly concrete mixtures.

stories.title: ICON Begins 3D Printing Its Largest Commercial Building for ASCO Equipment in San Antonio - https://3dprinting.com/
FKM reports productivity gains with EOS platform
stories.summary: FKM Additive Manufacturing reported a 67 percent increase in productivity using an unreleased EOS polymer platform. Build time for an in-house component dropped from over three hours to under two hours. The case study highlights productivity and repeatability as critical success factors for the company's additive series production.

stories.title: Crosslam completes six-storey timber apartment block
stories.summary: Crosslam has developed Aurora 275 in Suzano, which it claims is Brazil's tallest timber apartment block. The company, previously a supplier for over 300 projects, decided to build its own development to demonstrate the viability of timber construction. Brazil's list of engineered timber buildings continues to grow.

stories.title: CEPT University students develop AI safety tools
stories.summary: Students at CEPT University are testing AI-based construction safety tools at sites in Ahmedabad. The Safe Guard project uses computer vision to monitor real-time safety conditions, including helmet detection and inventory tracking. The system processes live feeds from CCTV and Wi-Fi cameras across different work areas.

stories.title: CEPT students use AI to monitor construction site safety
stories.summary: Students at CEPT University have developed an AI-based system to monitor construction sites in real time. The project uses computer vision and deep learning to detect if workers are wearing helmets and protective vests. It aims to assist supervisors who struggle with manual safety checks on large sites.

stories.title: India expands seismic network with 100 new observatories
stories.summary: The Ministry of Earth Sciences is adding 100 seismological observatories to its national network. The expansion aims to improve detection of low-intensity tremors and lower the country's earthquake detection threshold to magnitude 2.5. Scientists expect to gain deeper insights into tectonic activity across the country.

stories.title: Green Bengal Summit discusses climate-resilient development
stories.summary: The Confederation of Indian Industry’s Indian Green Building Council hosted the Green Bengal Summit in Kolkata to discuss sustainable urban growth. Policymakers, architects, and sustainability experts gathered to deliberate on Net Zero carbon pathways, urban regeneration, and strategies for future-proofing the state against climate-related challenges.

stories.title: Air purifiers gain traction as urban air quality concerns rise
stories.summary: Rising air pollution levels in Indian cities have led to increased demand for home air purifiers. As residents turn to smart technology to manage air quality, the growing reliance on these devices highlights broader questions about the accessibility of clean air in urban environments.

stories.title: Guide to selecting energy-efficient geysers for winter
stories.summary: Choosing a water heater for the winter requires balancing household size with energy consumption. Models with 5-star ratings and features like glass-lined tanks are marketed to help reduce electricity usage. Experts suggest considering heating capacity and high-rise building compatibility before making a purchase.

stories.title: Crompton Arno Neo geyser marketed for energy efficiency
stories.summary: The Crompton Arno Neo 25-litre storage water heater is being promoted for its 5-star energy rating and three-level safety features. Designed for daily household use, the model aims to help consumers manage electricity consumption during the colder months. It is currently priced at 7,299 rupees.

stories.title: CII IGBC Green Bengal Summit 2026 Deliberated on Future-Proofing Bengal’s Built Landscapes through Sustainable and Clima
Green Bengal Summit charts roadmap for sustainable infrastructure
stories.summary: The CII IGBC Green Bengal Summit in Kolkata brought together industry leaders and urban planners to discuss Net Zero buildings and sustainable infrastructure. The event focused on the theme of future-proofing the region through integrated urban development and climate-resilient growth strategies.

stories.title: Experts discuss making Bengal cities climate-resilient
stories.summary: Urban planners and developers met at the Green Bengal Summit to address challenges like waterlogging, rising temperatures, and pollution. Discussions centered on how greener buildings and improved water management can help cities cope with the pressures of rapid urbanisation and changing climate conditions.

stories.title: Social spaces in cities are disappearing
stories.summary: As public spaces become increasingly commercialised or controlled, the informal areas that foster social interaction are in decline. Libraries, cafes, and public squares are losing their function as meeting points, leaving fewer places for residents to gather outside of home and work.

stories.title: Urban flooding linked to poor drainage and rapid growth
stories.summary: Urban flooding during the monsoon is often exacerbated by inadequate drainage and the loss of natural water bodies. Concrete surfaces prevent rainwater absorption, while encroached floodplains restrict water movement. These factors combine to create recurring waterlogging issues across many Indian cities.

stories.title: Karachi opens sponge park to manage monsoon rainwater
stories.summary: A new one-acre sponge park in Karachi has been designed to hold up to 100,000 gallons of rainwater. Developed by the WWF-Pakistan and local partners, the project aims to reduce surface run-off and demonstrate how urban green spaces can mitigate local flooding risks.

stories.title: Energy transition requires new approach to urban planning
stories.summary: Sustainable urban planning requires making consequential decisions about building orientation and material use long before construction begins. Integrating clean energy and efficient infrastructure at the community level is essential for long-term performance, according to experts in international energy diplomacy and architecture.

stories.title: COP31 leaders focus on urban climate resilience finance
stories.summary: National leaders and CEOs met at COP31 to accelerate investment in urban climate resilience and energy-efficient infrastructure. Organisers are prioritising building decarbonisation and early warning systems, arguing that climate commitments must translate into tangible protections for the communities where people live.

stories.title: Playbook urges cities to plan for wildfire recovery
stories.summary: A new report advises cities to establish partnerships with financial institutions to secure recovery funding after wildfires. The playbook suggests that removing policy barriers and planning for financial resilience are necessary steps to speed up the rebuilding process for affected communities.

stories.title: Urban planning often overlooks children's needs
stories.summary: Indian cities are frequently designed for adult convenience, with little consideration for children's safety or play. Exposure to pollution has led to increased respiratory issues among adolescents, while a lack of outdoor space limits physical activity. Children rarely feature in urban policy discourse.

stories.title: Accra passes bye-law to manage urban heat
stories.summary: The Accra Metropolitan Assembly has passed a green infrastructure bye-law and purchased heat sensors to prepare for extreme temperatures. These measures are part of a multi-year project to monitor local heat levels and improve urban planning as the city faces potential climate risks.

stories.title: Archeform BIM 1.1 targets small architecture practices
stories.summary: Archeform BIM 1.1 is a SketchUp extension priced at 199 euros per year. It allows users to manage existing, demolished, and new construction in a single model. The software aims to save time for small practices that would otherwise draw the same plans multiple times.

stories.title: Exclusive | Zacua Ventures Raises $135 Million For Heavy-Industry Technology Bets - WSJ
Construction searches held up better than architecture in 2026
stories.summary: SignalHire reports that construction searches fell 19.94 percent in the first half of 2026, while architecture searches dropped 74.45 percent. The resulting 54.51 point gap is the widest in the built environment group. The data suggests an industry preference for building over designing.

stories.summary: Top 10 Best Climate Tech Startups in India in 2027 Climate technology is emerging as one of the most important areas of innovation in India’s startup ecosystem. With rising temperatures, unpredictable rainfall, deteriorating air quality, increasing energy consumption, water shortages and growing waste generation, the demand for practical technologies that

stories.title: Bedrock Robotics raises $600 million for autonomous excavators
stories.summary: Bedrock Robotics has raised $600 million in Series C financing, valuing the company at $4.1 billion. The firm aims to address labor shortages in commercial construction through autonomous equipment. The round brings total funding to nearly $1 billion, despite the company having yet to solve the labor shortage.

stories.title: AI agent makes laser-scanned buildings searchable
stories.summary: Austrian startup qapture has launched qentin, an AI agent that allows facility managers to search laser-scanned digital twins using natural language. The software has been tested on 38 Ikea sites. It promises to make finding fire extinguishers and equipment tags easier for those who have already scanned their buildings.

stories.title: Inc42, DevX Launch RE:FRAME With ₹15 Cr Investment Pool For PropTech Startups
stories.summary: India's real estate industry is worth an estimated $650 Bn. Yet, for a sector of this scale, the way properties are built, bought, sold and managed remains surprisingly dependent on traditional processes. From fragmented broker networks and manual verification to lengthy property transactions and construction inefficiencies, large parts of the

stories.title: SketchUp add-on brings BIM to smaller practices
stories.summary: Archeform BIM has released version 1.1 of its SketchUp extension, focusing on renovation workflows. The tool allows users to model walls, slabs and stairs as BIM elements that carry IFC data. It aims to put permit-ready drawings within reach of smaller practices that do not use enterprise software.

stories.title: Facilities management struggles with AI readiness
stories.summary: A survey of facilities management organisations found that while over half consider digital transformation highly important, only 24 percent rate themselves as AI-ready. Respondents cited cost pressures and integration challenges as primary hurdles. The industry is currently preparing to prepare for the future of maintenance.

stories.title: Architectural Competitions: Creativity and Career Growth
stories.summary: Architectural competitions occupy a distinctive place in the profession. They offer architects an opportunity to explore ideas beyond the limits of routine commissions, respond to challenging briefs, and present proposals to a wider audience. For emerging practices in particular, competitions can provide visibility and a chance to demonstrate their approach

stories.title: CEPT University updates BDes admission criteria
stories.summary: CEPT University will accept UCEED 2027 and NID DAT 2027 scores for its five-year Bachelor of Design programme. Candidates with valid scores in these national exams will be exempted from the university's own entrance test. The change applies to the 2027 academic session.

stories.summary: UNIVERSITY PARK, Pa. , Penn State will celebrate its 12th GivingTuesday on Dec. 1, and the College of Arts and Architecture invites alumni and friends to be a part of the event by making a gift to one or more of 18 campaigns across the college, benefiting student success, engaged

stories.title: Architecture faces a worker shortage
stories.summary: The construction industry needs 349,000 net new workers in 2026 to meet demand, according to the Associated Builders and Contractors. Women make up 47 percent of licensure candidates in architecture, yet the industry continues to struggle with retention. The solution is reportedly sitting in plain sight.

stories.title: GATE 2027 exam data to be published
stories.summary: IIT Madras will publish the number of students who appeared for the GATE 2027 exam on its official website. In 2026, there were 1,011,719 registrations and 797,434 actual test-takers. The authority will conduct the 2027 exams throughout February.

stories.summary: Madrid, ES IE School of Architecture & Design (IE University) will host raumlaborberlin at its campus in Madrid on November 25, 2026, at 6:00 PM, as part of its 2026 to 2027 COMMON(S) lecture series. Represented by Benjamin Foerster-Baldenius, the Berlin-based architecture collective will present “In the Flow of Making,”

stories.summary: Umeå School of Architecture (UMA) warmly welcomes employees, students and the public to a lecture titled Architects in Practice with Alejandro Haiek Coll and Toms Kokins as part of the open lecture series UMA Talks. research.title: Scientists capture electrons making seemingly impossible quantum jumps
research.summary: Scientists have captured electrons making seemingly impossible jumps across forbidden energy gaps in graphene, with some transitions occurring at a remarkable 100% probability. The breakthrough offers an unprecedented look at quantum behavior and could help unlock a new generation of ultrafast, light-controlled electronics.

research.title: Scientists discover a surprisingly simple way to turn coffee waste into fuel
research.summary: Scientists have developed an efficient method to transform used coffee grounds into a potential source of biodiesel while preserving the leftover material for other renewable fuels and valuable chemicals. The discovery could turn millions of tons of discarded coffee waste into a surprisingly useful resource for sustainable energy.

research.title: Superheated magma could fuel towering lava fountains
research.summary: Why do some volcanoes erupt with spectacular lava fountains while others release lava more quietly? Scientists have discovered that a hidden effect of extreme heat inside magma may help explain the difference. Experiments revealed that superheated magma can delay crystal formation for more than eight hours, compared with.

research.title: The Sun unleashed a monster storm. Earth may have made it worse
research.summary: The massive solar storm that illuminated skies worldwide in May 2024 has uncovered an unexpected twist: Earth's own atmosphere may have helped make the storm so powerful.
